stem: Input EC is stable, but root-zone EC rises as containers are allowed to dry much more deeply between irrigations. Which interpretation is strongest?
choices: A fertilizer-concentrate change remains the leading explanation even though the measured input EC is stable
Lower root-zone water content can concentrate dissolved ions, so dryback and salt accumulation should be evaluated together
The rising EC is most consistent with developing root disease because disease commonly increases conductivity during dryback
A source-water pH shift is the primary explanation because root-zone EC generally follows irrigation-water acidity
rationale: As root-zone water content declines, dissolved ions can become more concentrated. EC trends should therefore be interpreted together with moisture status and irrigation behavior.
